title: Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing for Calibrated Ensemble Weather Forecasts

contributions.purpose: Establish that AI weather forecast errors have significant directional (anisotropic) structure.
contributions.mechanism: Compute a calibration anisotropy index A_cal from spherical-harmonic coefficients of GraphCast Z500 residuals by partitioning modes into low-mu (zonal) and high-mu (meridional) bins via the normalized order ratio mu = |m|/l.
contributions.evaluation: GraphCast Z500 errors show A_cal = -0.276 +/- 0.005 (far beyond isotropy threshold 0.1); low-mu zonal modes contain 4.26x more power than high-mu meridional modes; strongest at synoptic scales (ratio 5.99).
contributions.domain: Data-driven weather forecasting / forecast error spectral analysis
contributions.source_quote: First, we demonstrate that GraphCast Z500 forecast errors exhibit significant quasi-zonal anisotropy (Acal = -0.276), with zonal modes containing 4.26x more power than meridional modes.

contributions.purpose: Convert deterministic AI forecasts into calibrated probabilistic ensembles by exploiting anisotropy.
contributions.mechanism: Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing (ASED): a training-free method extending spectral error dressing by modeling within-degree anisotropy via mu-binning (3 mu-bins) across 4 degree bands, redistributing variance across orders m while preserving the degree spectrum C_l; generates M=50 ensemble members.
contributions.evaluation: Uses odd/even month calibration/evaluation split (354 forecasts); requires no model retraining beyond bin weights.
contributions.domain: Ensemble generation / post-processing for AI weather models
contributions.source_quote: Second, we propose ASED, a training-free post-processing method that models within-degree anisotropy via mu-binning and multi-band degree decomposition.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that modeling directional error structure improves probabilistic calibration.
contributions.mechanism: Compare ASED against Deterministic, Isotropic GP, and standard SED baselines (with IFS-ENS as context reference) on WeatherBench2 Z500 at 5-day lead, using CRPS and Spread-Skill Ratio.
contributions.evaluation: Global CRPS 139.60 vs SED 143.80 (2.92% improvement, exceeds pre-registered 1% threshold); 82.4% of gridpoints improve; SSR moves 1.129 -> 1.123 toward 1.0.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we achieve 2.92% global CRPS improvement over SED on WeatherBench2, with 82.4% of gridpoints showing improvement, demonstrating that exploiting directional error structure meaningfully improves probabilistic calibration.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our ASED method builds on spectral error dressing by introducing within-degree anisotropy modeling via the mu = |m|/l parameterization.
ASED extends SED by redistributing variance across orders m while preserving the degree spectrum Cl.
This interpretation follows from the plane-wave analogy where kzonal ~ |m| and kmeridional ~ sqrt(l(l+1) - m^2) (Subich et al., 2025).

Standard Spectral Error Dressing (SED) samples perturbations with variance matching Cl, treating all orders m within each degree l as having equal expected power. This corresponds to an isotropic Gaussian random field on the sphere (Lang & Schwab, 2015).

notes: Mixed/partial result: extra-tropics CRPS improvement (0.75%) falls below the 1% threshold, and largest gains occur in tropics rather than the hypothesized extra-tropical storm tracks; substantial residual gap to physics-based IFS-ENS (117.34 vs 139.60). SED and Isotropic GP achieve similar CRPS (143.80 vs 143.47).
